diagnosis: The damped-oscillator model reproduces the ring-down across the full 80 min window. Standardised residuals are consistent with the assumed additive noise model for the single observable, with no structure in time, and no structural-misfit indicator fired. The likelihood profile for omega is smooth and closes on both sides well inside the declared bounds of 0.5 and 6.0, so the natural frequency is practically identifiable from this dataset. zeta and sigma are likewise bounded. Two limitations belong on the record. First, the estimate rests on in-sample fit and profile likelihood alone: there is a single experimental condition, so nothing could be held out and no predictive check was run. Second, and specific to this problem, the objective is multimodal in omega — the sampling interval of 1.6 min is comparable to the 3.3 min period, and several frequencies fit the sampled points well. The reported optimum is the best of 100 starts; a run with materially fewer starts could converge into one of the other basins, and the profile would then close around a wrong frequency and look exactly as clean as this one does.
cannot_distinguish: the natural frequency from its aliases under this sampling design — the interval reported here is conditional on the optimiser having found the deepest basin, which multistart evidence supports but a single-start fit would not; a finer sampling interval, not a better optimiser, is what would remove the ambiguity from the data itself

answers_intent.criterion: omega recovered within 5% of the value the data supports
answers_intent.evidence: The multistart optimum sits at omega = 1.900 rad/min. The profile over omega has its minimum at the same point, and the neighbouring local minima in the scanned range are separated from it by a likelihood difference far larger than the ratio threshold, so the selected basin is the deepest one this dataset supports.

answers_intent.criterion: profile CI for omega finite and narrower than one decade
answers_intent.evidence: The profile likelihood for omega closes on both sides at the likelihood-ratio threshold inside the declared bounds rather than running into them, giving a finite interval far narrower than one decade.
